title: Ultimate ROM File Compression Guide (CHD, PBP, and RVZ)
summary: Retro Game Corps explains CHD, PBP and RVZ as different storage choices for disc-based libraries, including PS2 images and GameCube/Wii titles.
searchKeywords: Ultimate ROM File Compression Guide (CHD, PBP, and RVZ)

blocks.text: Disc-image compression is not one universal format. This guide compares CHD, PBP and RVZ across systems such as PlayStation, PlayStation 2, Sega CD, GameCube and Wii, with a written companion and chapter markers. The useful distinction is between preserving the source disc layout and choosing a format supported by the emulator that will read it. A smaller file is only helpful if tracks, metadata and game behavior survive conversion.

Work from a personal disc dump and preserve the original image until the compressed copy has been verified. Check that the target emulator accepts the format, boot a title past the opening screen and compare hashes or use the format's own verification command where available. Multi-track CDs need particular care because a single data file is not always the whole disc. The video gives an organizing workflow; it does not make every format appropriate for every platform or emulator.
